mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or at least equal to the 5-day rolling mean during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 5,000 since the previous month's peak is associated with stronger consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase ≥5,000 since last peak
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns both negative, or no statistically significant correlation (p>0.1) between PAYEMS change and SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at an annualized rate exceeding 2% over the prior quarter, it indicates robust demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns in the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the p-value for the regression of returns on GDPC1 growth is >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index by more than 10% from the prior month suggests supply-side weakness, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline >10% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 4% with no reversal signal produces an expectation of higher inflation and tighter credit, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for the next 60 days with no change in SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment) below 3.5% triggers a labor market tightening that increases investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative or the change in UNRATE is not statistically significant with respect to SPX returns (p>0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 10% in the prior quarter compared to the previous quarter, it signals rebuilding demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST quarterly growth ≥10% vs prior quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or no significant relationship detected (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (labor) by at least 0.5% and 0.2% respectively over the prior month indicates dual pressure: higher rates reduce discounting while tighter labor markets boost sentiment, producing mixed but statistically significant positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↓0.5% AND UNRATE ↓0.2% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a two-variable regression.
